hook.line: Listen to people in Bogotá for an afternoon and you will hear *de pronto* and *igual* all the time, and neither means what the dictionary says. In everyday speech, both mean *maybe*.

examples.en: He might not come, I don't know.

rule:
In Colombia, *de pronto* at the start of a sentence means *maybe*, not only "suddenly". *Igual* at the start also means *maybe*, in casual talk.

Both work like *a lo mejor*: they are followed by the plain verb, no wish form. *De pronto llueve*, *Igual no viene*.

Watch out for *igual* as "the same" (*Me da igual*, *Es igual*). When it opens a sentence and a verb follows, it is *maybe*.

They are casual. For a polite or written *maybe*, use *a lo mejor* or *quizás*. In another country, people will understand you but may not say it themselves.
smallPrint: Teachers call these colloquial adverbs of possibility. Like *a lo mejor*, they take the indicative.

options: He might not come, I don't know.

readAndPick.es: De pronto Altamira quiere hablar con nosotros.
options: Altamira doesn't want to talk to us.
Maybe Altamira wants to talk to us.
Altamira wanted to talk to me.
There are lots of customers today.
Maybe there won't be customers today.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, using *de pronto*: Maybe it'll rain later.
yourTurn.why: *De pronto* opens the sentence, and the plain verb follows.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, using *igual*: Maybe Hernando is hungry.
yourTurn.why: *Igual* at the start means maybe, and the verb stays plain: *tiene*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *viene* or *venga* and type the whole sentence: *De pronto Vale ___ mañana.*
yourTurn.why: Like *a lo mejor*, *de pronto* takes the plain verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, using *igual*: Maybe we won't open tomorrow.
yourTurn.why: The *no* goes right before the verb, after *igual*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend, using *de pronto*: Maybe you're right.
Type in Spanish, using *igual*: Maybe it isn't true.
Say the same thing with *a lo mejor*: *De pronto Mariana sabe algo.*
yourTurn.answer: A lo mejor Mariana sabe algo.
yourTurn.why: The three work alike: all take the plain verb.
